title: AutoGPT Platform -- T1059 Redis cache pickle deserialization RCE
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-33233 (GHSA-rfg2-37xq-w4m9,
CVSS 7.6 HIGH), a self-reported advisory for AutoGPT Platform, versions
0.6.34 through 0.6.51.

The backend's cache layer (`cache.py`, near line 192) writes values to
Redis with `pickle.dumps(...)` and reads them back with a bare
`pickle.loads(cached_bytes)` -- no HMAC/signature check and no strict
schema validation gates the deserialization. Python's `pickle` protocol
executes arbitrary code during unpickling via an object's `__reduce__`
method; the advisory's own PoC uses a crafted class that, when
deserialized, creates the file `/tmp/autogpt_pickle_rce_official` as
proof of command execution. Any attacker able to write to the shared
Redis cache key -- whether through a separate Redis-access
vulnerability, a misconfigured/exposed Redis instance, or another
service sharing the same cache -- can trigger arbitrary command
execution in the backend container simply by having their poisoned
bytes read back through the normal cache-read path.

Detection logic flags the resulting host-level artifact: a Python
process attributed to the AutoGPT backend spawning a child process as a
direct consequence of a cache read -- since legitimate cache reads
never spawn subprocesses, any subprocess creation immediately following
a `cache.py` read call in the same process is the anomaly this bug
makes possible.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory
(Significant-Gravitas, via GHSA and NVD), fixed in 0.6.52 (moves to a
non-code-executing serialization format with schema validation; the
advisory also recommends HMAC-signing cached values and hardening the
Redis deployment itself -- auth, TLS, network isolation).
